Observatory

What can I see tonight?

What can I see?When can I see it?Where can I see it from?

The Observatory brings together Today's Sky, an interactive sky map, the Moon, planets, constellations, deep-sky objects, astronomical events and live space weather. Positions are calculated in your browser for the place and time you choose, and every panel says whether it is calculated, stored, live or an estimate.

Open the Observatory

The graphic beside this text is illustrative only; the Observatory itself shows real calculated sky positions.

Missions

From concept to discovery.

The Mission system is planned to cover active, historic and upcoming missions as a connected visual journey. A small, sourced sample (5 missions, 8 launches) is live in the Missions module; the full catalogue is not populated yet. The timeline below is the concept outline.

VAYUSH AI

Source-based answers, by design.

VAYUSH AI is a planned capability for scientific questions, research assistance and data interpretation. No assistant exists yet — below is the intended architecture.

  1. User question
  2. VAYUSH AI → entity & intent detection
  3. Relevant data retrievalVAYUSH database · scientific sources · research archive · approved external data
  4. Context generation
  5. AI responseExplanation + data + sources

Astronomy Tools

Calculators run in your browser on one shared calculation engine. Each shows its formula, assumptions and, where the dataset has a value, a check against it. Educational, not ephemeris-grade.

      About

      VAYUSH SPACE RESEARCH LABS

      Exploring Beyond Tomorrow.

      VAYUSH SPACE RESEARCH LABS is an independent digital space-science project focused on improving how people explore, learn and interact with space science, astronomy and scientific information.

      Focus

      AstronomySpace scienceScientific researchSpace missionsAstronomical observationScientific datasetsInteractive educationAstronomy tools3D visualizationAI-assisted explorationDigital research archives

      The aim is a digital space research environment where complex information becomes more accessible, interactive, visual, understandable, discoverable and data-driven.

      Vision

      Discover → Explore → Observe → Learn → Analyze → Research

      Scientific information, visualizations, tools and exploration connected in one unified environment.

      Scientific philosophy

      Science firstExperience firstPerformance firstModularity firstMobile firstSource firstBuild for the future

      VAYUSH distinguishes observed data, scientific interpretation and VAYUSH educational explanation, and tracks provenance wherever practical.

      Roadmap & data status

      VAYUSH is built in phases. The current build is a structure-first release: complete platform structure proven with small sourced sample data. Large datasets arrive in later phases. See Data & integrity for the live checks and source registry.

        V4.0.0 information depth. This release adds scientific context to existing records without adding any record. Every Explore record has a collapsible “Scientific depth” section: type-level background, arithmetic on the record’s own numbers (labelled derived), and relationships to other existing records. A set of flagship records also has an entity-specific profile with its own sources and a verification note. Rockets, satellites, spacecraft, missions, instruments, orbits and calculators gained context and worked examples. Most records still hold short summaries, and the profiles are an editorial synthesis whose cited papers were not all re-read in full; see each record’s evidence note. Phase statuses above are unchanged.
